transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lisa Gomez (Argon - Head of MLOps), Rajiv Menon (Argon - Dir AI Eng), Tom Harris (Argon - Procurement)
Recording note: auto-transcript with occasional mis-hearings (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Redwood de-di-cat-ed).

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um quick intros? Maya here, AE on the Redwood side.
[00:07] Lisa Gomez: hi, lisa here, head of mloops at Argon health. we run several inference pipelines for clinical summarization and triage.
[00:14] Rajiv Menon: rajiv, director of ai eng, i mostly care about latency and cost per convo.
[00:19] Tom Harris: tom from procurement, i'll ask the contracting questions later.
[00:22] Ethan Brooks: ethan, se at redwood, i'll own the benchmarks and perf stuff.

[00:30] Maya Patel: high level agenda — we want to size the workload, define success criteria for the POC, talk bench plan and where you expect to run (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and then commercial guardrails — credits, pilot length, allowed capacity and path to contract. sound right?

[00:47] Lisa Gomez: yes, that's right. a quick bit of context: our workload is chat-like summarization of patient notes, typical payload ~1.2k tokens, sometimes up to 2.5k. peak qps for regional testing is about 60 QPS, but realistic steady is 10-15.

[01:05] Ethan Brooks: ok that's helpful, so tokens per second and kv cache behavior will matter. do you currently use any prefix-caching or reuse tokens across requests?

[01:12] Rajiv Menon: we do some session-level caching in our app, but not KV cache at the model layer. the main constraint is P95 latency under 400 ms for interactive triage flows.

[01:22] Maya Patel: good. for the POC we usually propose a few discrete success criteria — throughput target (e.g., sustain 50 QPS with P95 < 500ms), quality guardrail (no regression on the evaluation prompt set), and operational criteria (integration with SSO and audit logging). what are your must-haves?

[01:38] Lisa Gomez: must-haves: P95 latency below 500ms for typical 1.2k token requests, model outputs pass our clinical safety prompts, and logs/audit for 30 days. optional is private deployment if SOC2+ and KMS required.

[01:50] Ethan Brooks: noted. for private we have Redwood Private (VPC) — sometimes transcript shows as privet — that supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering but it'll add network lead time.

[02:00] Tom Harris: network lead time — what ballpark? our legal wants to know procurement slippage risk.

[02:05] Ethan Brooks: for standard hosted POC, you can be up in a day. Dedicated or Private — plan on 3-6 weeks for networking, security review, and certs depending on infra.

[02:18] Rajiv Menon: ok procurement likely needs a firm pilot timeframe and an estimate of spend. how do you typically structure credits and what are limits?

[02:26] Maya Patel: typical pilot credit structure: we give a pool of credits that map to token usage and a timebox (30 or 60 days). credits cover hosted API usage and basic infra. Dedicated/Private may require a small reserved capacity commit or a separate price add. we can propose a 45-day pilot with $15k of credits to cover baseline benching and integration work — that's illustrative.

[02:45] Lisa Gomez: will credits cover stress tests? we will run high QPS spikes as part of bench.

[02:49] Ethan Brooks: yes the credit pool can be used for load tests. we just ask that you let us know planned test windows so we can monitor and temporarily increase limits for safety. also, for heavy sustained loads we recommend Dedicated or burst capacity to control latency.

[03:05] Maya Patel: important commercial guardrail: test accounts are rate-limited by default, we can relax during scheduled bench windows. pilot terms also include a clause around excessive training-like usage — i.e., no model fine-tuning against our hosted endpoints during the pilot unless explicitly agreed.

[03:20] Lisa Gomez: understood. on success metrics — you mentioned quality regression tests; can SE run the evals or do we run locally?

[03:27] Ethan Brooks: both. we'll run a Redwood-bench locally against samples you provide, and we recommend you run your gold prompts. SE will produce a quality report comparing baseline to pilot model variant.

[03:39] Rajiv Menon: for throughput benching, what's the suggested test matrix? e.g., payload sizes, concurrency, and cold-start vs warm cache?

[03:46] Ethan Brooks: suggested matrix: small (200-400 tokens), medium (1k-1.5k), large (2k+), concurrency sweep at 1, 5, 15, 30, 60 QPS. include warm vs cold runs to measure KV cache impact. we'll also measure tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens for comparison versus your current provider.

[04:05] Tom Harris: on procurement path: after pilot, do we get a standard MSA? SLAs?

[04:10] Maya Patel: yes — for enterprise we offer an MSA and schedule of services. Dedicated deployments come with SLA-backed latency targets and uptimes. We'll connect you to our contracts team after technical signoff. typical procurement timeline after pilot (assuming success) is 4-8 weeks depending on procurement load.

[04:25] Lisa Gomez: any compliance docs you can share? SOC2, ISO, encryption details?

[04:29] Maya Patel: yes — i'll send our security pack (SOC2 report, encryption and key management FAQs, data residency options). note: private deployments can use your KMS and on-prem options if needed.

[04:40] Rajiv Menon: curious on cost controls — how do we avoid surprise bills if we run a stress test?

[04:45] Ethan Brooks: we enforce quotas and spending caps at the account level. for pilots we set a hard credit limit and notify before overages. You can also set per-route caps in the Redwood Console.

[04:54] Lisa Gomez: what about model fallback? if you run out of capacity on a preferred model instance how do you maintain availability?

[04:59] Ethan Brooks: routing policies allow fallbacks to compatible model variants (lower compute or quantized variants). fallback is configurable and we can set them up for POC to ensure continuity.

[05:09] Maya Patel: let's align on concrete numbers for the bench run so AE can prepare credits. earlier you mentioned peak 60 QPS; is 60 the highest you'll test or more?

[05:18] Rajiv Menon: we'll spike to 80 QPS for resilience but sustained target is 50 QPS.

[05:24] Ethan Brooks: good to know. for hosted we can run the 80 QPS spike but for sustained 50 QPS with low p95 we'd recommend a small dedicated pool or tuned batching and kv cache. we'll quantify in the benchmark.

[05:35] Lisa Gomez: one more question on data: we have PHI — how does the hosted pilot handle that?

[05:40] Maya Patel: PHI is sensitive — for hosted we have data handling controls and SOC2, but many customers choose Redwood Private or VPC-hosted paths for PHI to keep keys and networking in their control. If you need, we can scope an on-prem or VPC pilot; that adds networking steps.

[05:54] Tom Harris: okay for procurement we need a written pilot terms doc with credit accounting, termination, and acceptance criteria. can we get that?

[05:59] Maya Patel: yes, AE will draft pilot terms and SOW. we'll include credit mapping (tokens -> credit units), pilot period, allowed test windows, and acceptance criteria.

[06:10] Ethan Brooks: technical note — please provide a sample of 500-1000 representative payloads and a small eval set (50 prompts) so we can run quality regressions and perf tests that reflect real usage.

[06:21] Lisa Gomez: we'll anonymize PHI and provide synthetic samples this week.

[06:25] Rajiv Menon: how do you measure cost in the benchmark report? cost per 1k tokens and cost per successful session?

[06:31] Ethan Brooks: yes we show cost per 1k tokens, tokens/sec, and an estimated cost per session (taking average token usage and average latency).

[06:38] Maya Patel: i'm going to summarize: SE runs the bench with your samples, AE sends pilot credit paper and SOW, customer confirms QPS and provides data samples, procurement shares timeline. after bench we reconvene to review results and confirm contracting path.

[06:50] Tom Harris: is there any non-disclosure we need before you ingest samples?

[06:54] Maya Patel: we can operate under a standard mutual NDA; if you prefer we can sign your NDA. we also have data handling addenda for PHI.

[07:02] Lisa Gomez: ok next steps sound good. timeline is tight — we'd like results in two weeks.

[07:08] Ethan Brooks: two weeks is feasible for a hosted benchmark; private will take longer. we'll aim to deliver initial bench results in 7-10 business days if we get samples and credentials this week.

[07:18] Rajiv Menon: for the bench spreadsheet, can you include comparison columns for our current provider (cost and p95)?

[07:23] Ethan Brooks: yes we'll include a comparison template — please populate your current provider numbers or we'll estimate.

[07:30] Maya Patel: any blockers from your side?

[07:33] Lisa Gomez: procurement wants 1) pilot terms doc, 2) security pack, and 3) clear credit accounting.

[07:38] Maya Patel: we'll deliver all three in the next 3 business days.

[07:42] Tom Harris: one last question — if pilot results are positive, how fast can you provision dedicated capacity and sign SLA?

[07:48] Maya Patel: if you choose Dedicated and negotiate terms quickly, provisioning is typically 2-4 weeks post-contract; SLA cycles with legal might extend that.

[07:56] Rajiv Menon: thanks everyone. can we reconvene on 2025-10-15 for review?

[08:00] Maya Patel: sounds good, i'll propose a calendar invite.

[08:05] Maya Patel (wrap): recap of next steps — (1) Ethan runs bench and shares sheet by 2025-10-09, (2) Maya to send pilot credit proposal, SOW and security pack by 2025-10-05, (3) Argon to provide anonymized samples and procurement timeline by 2025-10-07. action items captured. thanks all.

[08:20] End recording.

Notes on transcript quality: occasionally speaker labels switched, some product names transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache labelled KC cache, Redwood Private as privet). There are natural disfluencies and overlaps in the middle sections during Q&A.
